claims.claim: The interviewer places Hobb's writing closer to slice-of-life than to action, with fights serving character rather than plot.
claims.quote: closer the slice-of-life style than to action

claims.claim: Her research prefers diaries, journals and other primary documents over histories.
claims.quote: diaries, journals and things of that sort

claims.claim: She booked time aboard tall ships to get the smells and sensations of a sailing vessel.
claims.quote: the smells and sensations of a sailing vessel

claims.claim: She writes from questions, not answers, and dislikes message stories.
claims.quote: I do not care for 'message' stories

claims.claim: Events in one place inevitably have repercussions elsewhere in the world.
claims.quote: inevitably have repercussions in the Six Duchies

claims.claim: She wrote one novel in first-person present tense and will never attempt it again.
claims.quote: something I will NEVER attempt again

claims.claim: She wanted the world's deep history to unfold slowly.
claims.quote: I wanted it to unfold slowly

claims.claim: Each viewpoint reports its own sensory self-interest, as a dog cares how much butter is on the popcorn.
claims.quote: how much butter is on the popcorn

claims.claim: Fitz's voice kept taking her over even in emails, which is why Tawny Man followed Liveship.
claims.quote: even when I was writing e-mails

claims.claim: Her writing log records researching diseases of sheep and inserting chapter headings as bridge scaffolding.
Erikson admired the controlled point of view and leisurely pace, then found it a quiet seduction that set up the dog scene.
claims.quote: the controlled point of view, the leisurely pace

claims.feature: knowledge fed at a child's pace
claims.claim: The child narrator lets world-knowledge be fed piecemeal at a child's pace of comprehension.
claims.quote: at a child's pace of comprehension

claims.feature: first person unusual in epic fantasy
claims.claim: First person is an unusual approach in epic fantasy and gives complete immersion in Fitz's personality.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: complete immersion in Fitz's complicated personality

claims.claim: Withywoods values handkerchiefs, beeswax candles and lace as objects, a milieu likened to the Little House books.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: the objects of daily life are concrete and treasured

claims.claim: Conversations turn to herbs, crop seasons and fair treatment of servants rather than battle.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: the uses of herbs, the seasons for crops
